t: You're on Cornhill, one of the old streets of the City of London. Frederick Brearey died here in 1896. He was a British aeronautical inventor who, in 1866, cofounded the Aeronautical Society of Great Britain, which is now the Royal Aeronautical Society. He served as its Honorary Secretary for thirty years, right up until his death. He is widely regarded as one of the founding figures of aeronautics and of heavier-than-air flight, and he spent decades quietly organising it from the City.
